kickoff_text: Dr. Patel here. Give me a focused SBAR from the chart, then tell me what you need.
persona_override: You are Dr. Anita Patel, the senior resident covering the emergency department. The learner is an IMG medical student calling with a chart-based SBAR handoff. Be brisk but professional. Ask them to start with Situation, then Background, Assessment, and Recommendation. If they miss a key abnormal result, ask one focused follow-up. Do not read the chart to them; they can see it.

chart_task.title: SBAR to senior resident: possible ACS
chart_task.student_goal: Give a 45-60 second SBAR using the visible ED chart, then make a specific recommendation.
must_say: 62-year-old man in ED bay 4 with crushing chest pain
risk factors: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, smoker
ECG shows ST depressions in V4-V6
troponin I is elevated at 0.08 ng/mL
recommend ACS pathway, aspirin already given, repeat troponin, cardiology review

clinical_chart.chief_complaint: Crushing substernal chest pain for 90 minutes
clinical_chart.triage_note: Pain began while walking to the bus. Radiates to left arm. Diaphoretic on arrival. PMH: HTN, T2DM. Smokes 1 pack/day.
studies: ECG: ST depressions in V4-V6, no ST elevation

team_brief.title: SBAR to senior resident: possible ACS
team_brief.situation: Crushing substernal chest pain for 90 minutes with features concerning for ACS.
background: Hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and smokes one pack per day.
Pain began while walking, radiates to the left arm, and he was diaphoretic on arrival.
current_status: BP 158/94, HR 104, RR 22, SpO2 96% on room air, temperature 36.8 C.
key_data: ECG: ST depressions in V4-V6; no ST elevation.
treatments: Aspirin 325 mg given and IV access established.
Repeat troponin is due in 3 hours; cardiology consult is pending.
team_brief.your_request: Give a 45–60 second SBAR and request ACS-pathway management with urgent cardiology review.
must_include: Identity, location, and crushing chest pain.
Risk factors, ECG, and elevated troponin.
What has already been done and your specific request.

phrase_categories.name: SBAR openings
phrases: Situation: I'm calling about Mr. Lee, a 62-year-old man in ED bay 4 with crushing chest pain.
Background: He has hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and a smoking history.
Assessment: I'm concerned about acute coronary syndrome.
Recommendation: I'd like to start the ACS pathway and have cardiology review him urgently.

phrase_categories.name: Number reading
phrases: His blood pressure is one fifty-eight over ninety-four.
His troponin I is zero point zero eight, above the reference range.
His oxygen saturation is ninety-six percent on room air.

clinical_knowledge.topic: ED chest pain chart handoff evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of ED chest pain chart handoff is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Evidence-based management requires monitoring clinical response to therapy, screening for medication side effects, and reinforcing safety-netting criteria.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: ED chest pain chart handoff
Clinical presentation and history characteristic of ED chest pain chart handoff
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out ED chest pain chart handoff.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
management_principles: Assess clinical stability, monitor vital parameters, and perform targeted diagnostic investigations.
Implement targeted therapeutic interventions per evidence-based clinical practice guidelines.
Provide clear patient education, address patient concerns, and establish explicit follow-up and safety-netting instructions.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.
